plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and dense spikes of fragrant purple flowers held above the leaves on slender stems. It thrives in full sun and well-drained soil and is a favorite of bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; widely cultivated in southern France, England, the United States, and Tasmania
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and the name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', since the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Rosa canina
plants.description: A vigorous, arching, thorny shrub of hedgerows and woodland edges bearing delicate, five-petaled, lightly scented flowers. The blooms are followed by bright red rose hips that are rich in vitamin C.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (June to July)
plants.location: Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia; naturalized in North America and Australia
plants.funFact: During World War II, British children collected dog rose hips to make vitamin C-rich syrup when citrus fruits were scarce.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial with strap-like leaves and tall, leafless stems topped with rounded umbels of trumpet-shaped blue flowers. Its early-summer bloom makes it popular in gardens and along roadsides in warm climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere in cultivation)
plants.location: Native to South Africa; cultivated worldwide in mild climates such as California, the Mediterranean, and Australia
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, Agapanthus is not a true lily; its name comes from the Greek 'agape' (love) and 'anthos' (flower).

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A dramatic evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, made up of showy pink bracts surrounding a central cone of tiny flowers. It grows in nutrient-poor, acidic soils in fynbos vegetation.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak bloom around May to September
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape regions of South Africa
plants.funFact: The King Protea is South Africa's national flower, and the genus is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change his shape, reflecting the plant's great diversity.
